name: Barren
overview: Scripture presents the condition of barrenness not as a final state of despair but as an opportunity for God’s intervention and blessing. In Genesis 25:21, Isaac’s prayer for his barren wife Rebekah results in God enabling her to conceive, demonstrating His power to open closed wombs. Psalms 113:9 and Isaiah 54:1 celebrate the transformation of barrenness into joy and multiplication, affirming that those who were once childless can become fruitful beyond expectation. The New Testament echoes this hope, with Luke 23:29 and Galatians 4:27 proclaiming blessings and rejoicing for the barren, pointing to a spiritual fulfillment that surpasses physical circumstances.
